Rendered for lab-vsrx-1 at 2026-11-24T21:00:00Z, after the lab gate on its own facts. Before unit 1, check that your CLI prompt shows labadmin@lab-vsrx-1.
LAB ONLY. This adds 'set system scripts language python3'. That lets any unsigned Python script owned by a super-user-class account run on this device's routing engine, not only J-Wicket: a change to the device's security posture. J-Wicket is not qualified for production (gate G1 has not passed). Continue only on a disposable lab device you are allowed to change.
LAB ONLY. With --access tls the runtime commit opens a new HTTPS listener on this device's management address: the --listen-address, by default --host, which the installer does not check is the management address (an address of a revenue interface would put the listener there; in the mgmt_junos routing instance when 'system management-instance' is set). It is reachable by anything that reaches that address: J-Wicket's sign-in page becomes one more way into this device, beside SSH and NETCONF. Its certificate is self-signed; compare its SHA-256 fingerprint in the browser with the one the installer prints. J-Wicket has not passed gate G1 or a security review (Q-SEC-01). Continue only on a lab device whose management network you control.
J-Wicket will run with the rights of labadmin, a super-user-class account that can commit configuration ('username labadmin' under 'system extensions extension-service application file jwicket.py'). A compromise of J-Wicket is a compromise of this device.
This adds 'set system services netconf ssh': NETCONF over SSH on TCP 830 and on the SSH port, reachable on fxp0 and on any interface whose security zone admits netconf (830) or ssh (22), not only J-Wicket's loopback session.
The netconf backend's reach to the device's own NETCONF ('show configuration system services netconf') rests on the probe (check C3) only: it is not checked end to end, because no check uses an SSH channel (SSH forwarding was refused on the lab SRX4100). Sign in once to prove it.
In an SSH or console session on the lab device (the shell is outside Juniper support; this is the one read the installers make there):

Unit 4 (file): the settings file (workstation) [file jwicket.ini]
Status: render_settings output; parsed by jwicket.settings in the tests; the TLS settings verified on SRX4100 25.2R1-S1.4 (deploy-lab TLS variant)
```
# /var/db/jwicket/jwicket.ini: J-Wicket settings, written by jwicket-install (lab only).
# Every value is checked before anything listens. J-Wicket listens with TLS on the device's
# management address (--access tls); run the installer again to change this file.

[server]
bind = 192.0.2.10
port = 9443
tls_cert = /var/db/jwicket/tls.crt
tls_key = /var/db/jwicket/tls.key
allowed_hosts = 192.0.2.10:9443

[auth]
backend = netconf

[log]
file = /var/db/jwicket/jwicket.log
audit_file = /var/db/jwicket/audit.jsonl
```

A self-signed RSA-2048 certificate for 192.0.2.10, made on the device so that its private key never leaves it. In an SSH session on the lab device as labadmin (not root):
Unit 6 (device-shell): the TLS certificate (on the device)
Status: verified on SRX4100 25.2R1-S1.4 (deploy-lab TLS variant); the shell openssl's version was not recorded (Python's ssl: OpenSSL 1.1.1zb); outside Juniper support
```
start shell sh
cd /var/db/jwicket
umask 077
openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -sha256 -days 90 -keyout tls.key -out tls.crt -subj /CN=192.0.2.10 -addext subjectAltName=IP:192.0.2.10
chmod 600 tls.key
chmod 644 tls.crt
openssl x509 -in tls.crt -noout -fingerprint -sha256
exit
```
Write down the 'SHA256 Fingerprint=' line it printed: the browser's certificate warning is checked against it (unit 'open the UI'). Never copy tls.key off the device.

The same for tls.key, and '-rw-r--r--' and 'labadmin' for tls.crt. If a mode is wrong: 'file change-permission /var/db/scripts/jet/jwicket.py permission 644' (and the same for the others); outside Juniper support, the shell's 'chmod' does the same.
